`budget.py` now takes an optional month: `python3 budget.py 2026-09` counts only September's transactions, and with no argument it prints exactly what it did before.

I ran it against your data:

| Envelope | No month (unchanged) | `2026-09` | `2026-08` |
|---|---|---|---|
| groceries | 174.60 | 371.55 | 403.05 |
| fuel | 22.85 | 124.75 | 78.10 |
| eating out | 45.75 | 84.25 | 111.50 |
| household | 54.61 | 101.60 | 73.01 |

- **Bad input:** the month must be written as `YYYY-MM`. Anything else (`2026-9`, `2026-13`, or more than one argument) prints an error and usage line to stderr and exits with code 2.
- **Empty months:** a valid month with no transactions, such as `2026-07`, shows every envelope at its full allocation rather than an error. A typo'd year will look like an untouched budget.
